INTEGRATION STATE — three parallel worktrees, all UNCOMMITTED. Read before touching any of them.

  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam  (feat/llm-provider-seam)  172e + resolve_model_string
  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-cc33           (feat/cc33-fallback)      cc33 COMPLETE
  /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-cb6f           (feat/cb6f-pointer)       cb6f COMPLETE

cc33: 15 tests, ONE attempt, 194 passing across every touched module, ruff+mypy clean. Built
should_fall_back (classifies at call time via classify_llm_failure, membership in
failure._RETRYABLE | {CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL} — so a taxonomy change propagates without editing
the feature), fallback_targets_for, build_fallback_model, entered_fallback_model, providers.model_for
with a scoped endpoint override, and the runner chain branch (capability intersection over the built
candidate objects, candidates + ran_model in provenance).

cb6f: 14 tests, ONE attempt. Doc gate verified by me independently (literal read, one table entry,
zero in the non-literal section, regeneration idempotent). read_reserved_section untouched.
Deep-merge mutation-checked: swapping it for dict.update fails exactly the nested-sibling and
array-replace tests.

=== THE TWO INTEGRATION RISKS ===

1. MODULE-SIZE PRESSURE IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. Cap is 800, absolute CI gate.
       runner.py    689 -> 782 in cc33   (18 lines headroom)
       config.py    777 -> 786 in cb6f   (14 lines headroom)
   7761 also targets the runner (the two batch runners + sizing), and 172e still needs the lazy
   resolve_model_string call in llm/config.py. EITHER could breach the cap once merged. Decide the
   split BEFORE writing more code into those two files — this is the third time this epic has hit
   saturation (runner.py twice already: tasks 2682 and 3a98, then ticket 1484 for gate_dispatch and
   orchestrator). Do not squeeze; split along an existing call-graph seam as those tickets did.

2. model_classes.py IS EDITED BY TWO WORKTREES from the same 212-line base:
       provider-seam  +31/-1    (resolve_model_string + the CLASS constants)
       cc33          +114/-4    (fallback construction)
   Both are largely appends so the merge should be mechanical, but it MUST be done deliberately —
   and the merged file needs its tests re-run TOGETHER, not just each worktree's own.

=== cc33's THREE FLAGGED JUDGMENT CALLS (its own words, worth reviewing) ===
a. The plan never said how the runner learns WHICH class it is running (172e/7761 own class
   selection and had not landed). It resolved this with fallback_targets_for(resolved) matching the
   resolved provider:model string back to its slot; first slot in CLASS_NAMES order wins on a tie.
   Least-coupled choice, but it was the agent's call, not the plan's — review it.
b. Capabilities computed from the built candidate MODEL OBJECTS rather than the strings, to preserve
   the S4 profile override (_RebarOpenAICompatibleProvider withdrawing supports_json_schema_output)
   that the single-model path already honours. Passing strings would have silently regressed it.
c. provider_provenance's provider/endpoint_host still describe the PRIMARY for a chain (provenance_for
   lives in capabilities.py, outside cc33's file boundary). candidates + ran_model are added alongside
   so nothing attests a model that did not run, but a strict reader could argue endpoint_host should
   follow the answering candidate. Left deliberately.
Also: it found providers.py's _build_bedrock docstring claiming "289/300 LOC" was ALREADY stale at 299
before it started, and reworded it to keep the guidance without the false number.

=== 172e's OPEN PLAN-LEVEL DECISION (blocks its completion) ===
My change makes the verifier resolve to "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6" where today it is the bare
"claude-sonnet-4-6". Same model, different STRING — and 172e's plan promises "byte-identical to today
for every existing deployment". It is not. Caught by an EXISTING test, not by mine. Either special-case
the unconfigured default to preserve byte-identity, or accept the qualified form and correct the plan's
claim (recommended — a qualified id is unambiguous and is what provenance wants). This changes what
172e PROMISES, so it needs a re-review, not an implementer's call. Full detail on ticket 172e.

compiled_state.description:
# Per-class fallback chains

## Context / Problem
A class may name a model that is not always reachable — a local endpoint that is down, a provider
being throttled. Today a single unreachable model fails the gate outright; there is no way to say
"use the local trivial model, but fall back to a hosted one".

## Approach
Consume the `fallback` array that the schema ticket already parses, constructing pydantic-ai's
`FallbackModel(default, *fallbacks, fallback_on=...)` per class. Fallback entries are INLINE model
configs (same shape as a slot), not references to named presets, so nothing requires the operator to
look up rebar vocabulary.

`fallback_on` must be set deliberately rather than left at its default. pydantic-ai's own docs warn
that provider SDK retry logic can delay failover substantially — a 429 may be retried inside the SDK
for up to ~60s before the fallback is ever reached — so the condition is narrowed to the errors where
switching providers actually helps (availability/rate-limit classes), not every exception.

**Alternative rejected — rebar-implemented retry/failover.** pydantic-ai already ships this and rebar
already depends on it; a second implementation would diverge from the runner's error taxonomy.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/` — construct `FallbackModel` from a class's fallback list where the model is built.
- `tests/unit/` — construction and selection tests.

## Testing
Unit tier with a stubbed model: no network, no live provider.
- a class with no `fallback` builds the plain model (no FallbackModel wrapper) — today's behaviour.
- a class with one fallback builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary.
- an error in the configured `fallback_on` class selects the fallback.
- an error OUTSIDE that class propagates instead of silently failing over.

## DECIDED — the five runtime questions, against the VERIFIED pydantic-ai API

The first revision of this section asserted mechanisms without checking pydantic-ai's actual surface,
and the review correctly blocked all three. Every claim below now cites the installed source at
`.venv/.../pydantic_ai/models/fallback.py` and `.../messages.py`.

**1. `endpoint` on a fallback entry IS honored.** `resolve_fallback_chain` returns `provider:model`
STRINGS, which structurally cannot carry an endpoint, so it is NOT the construction input — it stays
as the human-readable / provenance view. Construction consumes the full `FallbackTarget`
(`model` + `provider` + `endpoint`) and builds each entry through the same provider path as the
primary. Dropping it would defeat the main reason to configure a fallback (a local
OpenAI-compatible proxy backing a hosted primary).

**2 + 3. Lifecycle is SPLIT, and the split is the point.** VERIFIED: `FallbackModel.__aenter__`
(fallback.py:167) enters every sub-model through an `AsyncExitStack` and `__aexit__` closes them —
its own docstring says "Enter all sub-models so their providers can manage HTTP client lifecycle".
So clients created by pydantic-ai's OWN providers are pydantic-ai's to close, and the `FallbackModel`
MUST be used as an async context manager or those sub-providers are never entered at all.

That does NOT cover rebar-created transports. `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` constructs an
`httpx.AsyncClient` that REBAR owns and passes in; those still register on
`ProviderSession._closeables` (`providers.py:102`, appended at `:214`/`:276`, drained at `:289`), one
per Anthropic-typed entry. Rule: whoever CREATES the client closes it. Registering pydantic-ai's own
clients on `_closeables` would double-close; omitting rebar's would leak one per call.

**4. Capabilities are the conservative intersection, computed BEFORE the wrapper exists.** VERIFIED:
`FallbackModel` has no `.profile`; its `.provider` property returns `None` (fallback.py:191) and
`.base_url` returns `models[0].base_url`. So calling `capabilities_for()` on the wrapper — as
`runner.py:365` does today for a single model — would silently yield primary-flavoured or default
capabilities rather than failing. Therefore capabilities, cache settings and tool-capability guards
are computed from the RESOLVED CANDIDATE LIST (primary + every fallback) before the wrapper is built,
and a capability holds only if EVERY candidate has it. `capabilities_for` is never called on a
`FallbackModel`. Concretely: a chain containing Bedrock `claude-opus-4-8` (MEASURED
`supports_temperature: False`) withdraws `temperature` for the whole chain — otherwise the run
succeeds or raises depending on which candidate answered, a failure reproducing only under provider
degradation.

**5. `ran_model` comes from the RESPONSE, not from the model object.** VERIFIED:
`FallbackModel.model_name` (fallback.py:194) returns the synthetic combined string
`f"fallback:{...}"` and is USELESS for attestation. But `ModelResponse.model_name`
(`messages.py:2106`) carries the name of the model that actually produced the response. So
`provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` (known at build time) and `ran_model` read
from the returned `ModelResponse`. A verdict recording only the primary would ATTEST THE WRONG MODEL
whenever a fallback fired — the misattribution 343b exists to prevent, which this feature must not
reintroduce.

**6. `fallback_on` is a CALLABLE PREDICATE over the EXISTING retryable set.** Two errors in the
previous revision, both caught: (a) "derive from `ResolutionClass`" while also naming exception TYPES
was a category error — `_map()` classifies an INSTANCE into a class, it does not yield a tuple of
types; (b) the trigger set omitted `RETRY_NOW`, which is where `failure.py:259` maps
`httpx.ConnectError` / `httpx.ConnectTimeout` — i.e. A DOWN LOCAL ENDPOINT, the exact scenario this
ticket's opening sentence motivates. The chain would not have fired for its own primary use case.

VERIFIED resolution: `fallback_on` accepts a callable (fallback.py:92-107). rebar passes a predicate:

    fallback_on = lambda exc: classify(exc) in _RETRYABLE or classify(exc) is CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL

`_RETRYABLE` is the EXISTING frozenset at `failure.py:51` — `{WAIT_AND_RETRY, RETRY_NOW}` — not a new
list. That is what makes the no-drift claim true: a future taxonomy change updates the fallback
behaviour automatically, whereas any hand-maintained set (including the one this plan carried until
now) drifts silently.

What that covers, traced through `failure.py` rather than asserted:

| class | reached by | falls back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RETRY_NOW` | `httpx.ConnectError`, `ConnectTimeout` (:259) — a down endpoint | YES |
| `WAIT_AND_RETRY` | 429 rate-limit, 529, 5xx (:215-220); Read/Pool/Write timeouts (:261) | YES |
| `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` | `FallbackExceptionGroup` (:272), model-unavailable | YES |
| `CHANGE_SETTINGS` | 401/403 (:223), `UserError` | no |
| `CHANGE_INPUT` | 400 context-length, 413 (:225-228) | no |
| `INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS` | 402, and 429 WITH `insufficient_quota` (:216-217) | no |
| `FIX_AGENT_DESIGN`, `NEEDS_INVESTIGATION` | agent/schema defects | no |

Note the 429 SPLIT, which the review surfaced and a naive "429 -> fall back" rule gets wrong: a plain
rate-limit 429 is `WAIT_AND_RETRY` and DOES fall back, but a 429 whose body carries
`insufficient_quota` is `INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS` and does NOT. Rationale for excluding it: quota or
payment exhaustion is a SPEND problem, and silently relocating spend to another provider is worse
than failing loudly. This is a deliberate, arguable call — recorded here so it is revisited on
purpose rather than discovered by surprise.

Excluded for the same fail-loudly reason: `CHANGE_SETTINGS` (a credential problem must not be masked
by shopping for a provider whose key happens to work) and `CHANGE_INPUT` (another provider will not
fix an oversized request — the SIZE LADDER owns that path, and falling back would hide it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts a class without `fallback` builds an unwrapped model (no behaviour change)
- [ ] a test asserts a class with `fallback` builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error in the configured condition selects the fallback entry
- [ ] a test asserts an error outside the condition PROPAGATES rather than failing over
- [ ] the chosen `fallback_on` condition is documented in-code with the SDK-retry caveat

- [ ] a test asserts a fallback entry carrying `endpoint` produces a model object built against THAT
      endpoint — not one silently built against the provider default
- [ ] a test asserts every fallback client is registered on the SAME `ProviderSession` and is closed
      on teardown: with N Anthropic-typed fallbacks, `_closeables` holds N+1 clients and all are
      closed exactly once (this fails against a per-entry-session implementation, which leaks)
- [ ] a test asserts a chain containing a model with `supports_temperature: False` withdraws
      `temperature` for the WHOLE chain, not just when that model is the primary
- [ ] a test asserts `provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` AND a `ran_model` equal
      to the model that actually answered — so a verdict produced by a fallback does not attest the
      primary
- [ ] a test asserts `fallback_on` fires on a 429/529/5xx and on a transport error, and does NOT
      fire on 401/403 or on a 400 context-length error (the loud-failure cases)
- [ ] a test asserts the `fallback_on` predicate is derived from `failure.py`'s `_RETRYABLE`
      frozenset plus `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` — NOT a hand-maintained tuple of exception types
- [ ] a test asserts the predicate returns True for `httpx.ConnectError` (RETRY_NOW — the down-local-
      endpoint case this ticket exists for), True for a 529/5xx, and False for 401/403 and for a 400
      context-length error
- [ ] a test asserts the 429 SPLIT: a plain rate-limit 429 falls back, a 429 carrying
      `insufficient_quota` does NOT (it classifies as INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS)
- [ ] a test asserts `capabilities_for` is NEVER called with a `FallbackModel` instance (it has no
      `.profile` and its `.provider` is None, so it would silently return default capabilities)
- [ ] a test asserts `ran_model` is read from the returned `ModelResponse.model_name`, NOT from
      `FallbackModel.model_name` (which is the synthetic `fallback:a,b` string)
- [ ] a test asserts the `FallbackModel` is used as an async context manager, so its sub-models'
      providers are entered and exited (pydantic-ai closes ITS clients; rebar-created retrying
      transports remain on `ProviderSession._closeables`, closed exactly once, never double-closed)
